baslik: Hail Killed Both Engines and the Jet Landed on a Highway

sahneler.metin: A DC-9 with no working engines tried to land on a Georgia highway.
It crashed into roadside buildings, and seventy two people were killed.
The crew had flown into a severe thunderstorm.
Hail was so intense it broke the windshield.
Both engines swallowed massive amounts of water and hail.
Their compressors were wrecked, and both flamed out.
One board member blamed the decision to fly into the storm.
It remains Georgia's deadliest air crash.
